title: The Thorn of the Ninefold Court
premise: Casper Whitlock survives in the magic-outlawed city of Vell by stealing memories and bottling them as charms—until a client's purchased memory reveals Casper's own face in the Ninefold Prophecy, written a century before their birth. Hunted by the usurper Aldric Vane's inquisitors, who believe the prophecy's 'Thorn' can unmake his claim to the Ninefold Court, Casper flees with Wren, the memory-thief who became their lover and is secretly an agent of the old court. As armies march on the free cities, Casper learns the Thorn's power requires sacrificing every memory they have ever stolen—including the ones that made them who they are. In the end, Casper chooses to burn their stolen past to shatter Vane's legitimacy, keeping only one memory: Wren's face, proving love can outlast even the self.
about_author: Tamsin Quintana is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat on the estuary, where she claims the tide keeps her honest.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Hours
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper lifts a memory of first snowfall from a dying merchant and bottles it for sale, establishing the charm trade and the city's fear of magic. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness—Casper hoards memories they never lived because their own childhood was erased.

chapters.title: A Client Named Wren
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A charming stranger named Wren buys three memories of the sea and lingers over tea, flirting dangerously. Casper feels seen for the first time in years, but notices Wren watches their hands too closely—as if cataloguing a technique rather than admiring it.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Refused to Hold
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper breaks into the archive of the Ministry of Purity to erase a client's trail and finds a forbidden book: the Ninefold Prophecy. Their own face stares back from an illumination captioned 'the Thorn.' Terror replaces triumph as bells begin to ring below.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Inquisitor Seraphine Hale interrogates Casper gently, almost kindly, revealing she has been hunting the Thorn for a decade. Casper lies well enough to walk free but knows the net is closing; the beat is dread wrapped in courtesy.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Charms
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper burns their stock, says goodbye to the orphaned pickpockets who are the closest thing to family, and prepares to run alone. The emotional beat is grief for a life built on invisibility now forfeit.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Sea
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren intercepts Casper at the docks and confesses he serves the exiled heir of the Ninefold Court—and that he sought out the Thorn deliberately. Betrayal wars with attraction; Casper nearly gutters him but takes his hand instead.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Fleeing through the marshlands, Casper discovers stolen memories leak into their dreams as visions of the ancient war. Wren teaches them to anchor the leaks; intimacy deepens even as trust stays broken.

chapters.title: The Free City of Ashenford
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In Ashenford's refugee quarter, Casper meets the found family of the resistance: a disgraced court mage, twin smugglers, and a child who remembers everything she steals. For one night, Casper belongs somewhere.

chapters.title: Seraphine's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Seraphine. Hale interrogates a captured pickpocket and realizes Casper's true nature—not destroyer, but vessel. Her faith in Vane cracks as she reads what the usurper intends to do with the Thorn once caught.

chapters.title: Vane's Court
chapters.summary: POV Seraphine. At the usurper's capital, Seraphine witnesses Vane feed a captured mage's memories to a machine of iron and bone. She understands the war's true stakes and begins quietly compiling evidence against her master.

chapters.title: The Price of the Charm
chapters.summary: POV Casper. To save the smuggler twins from a Vane patrol, Casper uses the Thorn's power for the first time—unmaking the soldiers' loyalty memories. The cost: a year of Casper's own past dissolves, and Wren sees it happen.

chapters.title: What Wren Never Told
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren admits he was ordered to deliver Casper to the exiled heir alive—or not at all—and that his courtship began as assignment. Casper walks into the marshes alone; the beat is heartbreak without accusation.

chapters.title: The Heir in the Hollow Hill
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The exiled heir Ilsevet receives Casper in a hidden fortress and reveals the full prophecy: the Thorn must be emptied entirely to break Vane's blood-magic claim. Casper refuses to become a blank vessel for another crown.

chapters.title: Armies on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: POV Seraphine. Vane's legions burn the salt road toward Ashenford. Seraphine defects with her ledger, reaching the resistance half-dead, offering proof that Vane's claim rests on stolen royal memories—the same crime Casper is punished for surviving.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Purpose
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The resistance plans its defense; Casper trains with Ilsevet's mages while Wren keeps careful distance. When the child thief is endangered, Casper and Wren fight back-to-back without words—an apology written in motion.

chapters.title: The Siege of Ashenford
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Vane's army breaches the walls. Casper empties memory after memory to turn soldiers, growing hollow-eyed and strange, forgetting names mid-battle. Wren holds them upright and speaks their history aloud so they don't lose themselves completely.

chapters.title: Hale's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Seraphine. Inside Vane's command tent, Seraphine sabotages the memory-machine at the cost of her own career and nearly her life, escaping to warn Casper that Vane comes personally—for the Thorn, and for the machine's final component: Casper's heart's-blood.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Captured and brought before Vane, Casper is offered survival in exchange for willing service. Vane shows them the erased truth: Casper's childhood was taken by the old court itself. Every side, it seems, has fed on them.

chapters.title: Ninefold Breaking
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the climax atop the ruined Ninefold Court, Casper chooses the emptying—but on their own terms, releasing every stolen memory as a storm that unmakes Vane's fabricated claim before the assembled armies. The throne's legitimacy burns to ash with Casper's past.

chapters.title: One Memory Kept
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Casper wakes blank as winter, holding a single bottled charm they refused to release: Wren's face at first snowfall. Wren introduces himself again, terrified and hopeful; the beat is love beginning honestly, from nothing.

chapters.title: The Court That Chose
chapters.summary: POV Seraphine. With Vane dead and the old court discredited, the free cities convene to choose governance together. Seraphine testifies with her ledger; Ilsevet declines the crown. The age of thrones ends not with a coronation but with a vote.

chapters.title: First Snowfall, Again
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Months later, Casper—rebuilding a self from other people's stories—opens the last charm with Wren beside them and lives the memory fresh. Some things, the book suggests, are not remembered but chosen, season after season.
